newsitem.title: USA: Noven sees Q4 share loss of $0.11.
newsitem.headline: Noven sees Q4 share loss of $0.11.

text.p: Noven Pharmaceuticals Inc said Wednesday it experienced a loss of about $0.11 a share for the fourth quarter of 1996, resulting in a full-year loss per share of $0.10.
Noven issued the update to analysts, saying it plans reporting its year-end 1966 results as well as its outlook for 1997 on March 26.
It said its total revenues for 1996 were about $21.6 million. In 1995, it reported a loss of $0.34 a share and total revenues of $12.2 million, it said.

The company explained that although in-market sales on Noven's transdermal estrogen delivery system, Vivelle and Menorest, continue to increase globally, inventory balancing by its licensing partners will result in significantly lower reorder levels during the first half of 1997, causing losses.
After the balancing adjustment is made, Noven said it expects product sales to its licensing partners will significantly increase in the second half of 1997.

It said it further anticipates that the decline in sales of Vivelle and Menorest in 1997 will be offset by increasing revenues for its DentiPatch product and additional licensing revenues. That will result in profitability for the year, it said.

Steven Sablotsky, president and chairman of the comany, said, "Noven has positioned itself for high earnings growth based on an expanding hormone replacement therapy market, the national rollout of DentiPatch, the planned filing of our combination estrogen/progestogen product and numerous opportunities for products in our pipeline."
